name: table-2n-a
label: 2 ÷ 3 to 2 ÷ 49
text:
% Table of 2 divided by the odd numbers, entries 2 ÷ 3 to 2 ÷ 49. Chace vol. II pl. 2-15 (photographs I-IV), PDF pp. 51-78; Peet pp. 38-43 (Pl. A-B), summary table p. 37.
% Layout of each entry: the summary line at the top of the entry (red unit fraction of n, then in black what it gives) is
% written one pair to a row, in the papyrus's left-to-right order; the working columns follow, one column after another
% as Chace sets them out left to right. A row of three numbers "4  28  '4" is the scribe's double statement
% (4 times n is 28; '28 of n is '4); see Chace's note to 2 ÷ 7.
% Ticks: Chace prints the ticks of 2 ÷ 5, 2 ÷ 7 and 2 ÷ 9 in red; the notation does not colour a tick.
% Peet says (p. 38) that he corrected the fractional dots "without further comment" in these sums, so a dot
% that Peet has and Chace has not (or the reverse) is not listed below as a disagreement unless it matters; see the notes.

2 ÷ 3
{"Call"} "2 out of 3"
{2/3}  2

2 ÷ 5
"5"                 % the divisor, written in black above the working
{'3}  1 2/3
{'15}  '3
{"Working-out:"}
  1    5
  2/3  3 '3
\ '3   1 2/3        % Peet: 1 2/3, with the footnote "Wrongly given as 1 '3 in the plate" (Peet's own plate)
\ '15  '3

2 ÷ 7
{'4}  1 '2 '4
{'28}  '4
  1    7
  '2   3 '2
\ '4   1 '2 '4
\ 4    28   '4      % Chace: 28 written without the dot (two multiplications: 4 × 7 = 28, '28 of 7 = '4); Peet prints '28, footnote "Actually 28"
  1    7
  2    14
\ 4    28

2 ÷ 9
{6}  1 '2           % Chace: "The fractional dot is omitted in the first term of the answer ... this term is '6 and not the whole number 6"
{'18}  '2
  1    9
  2/3  6
  '3   3
\ '6   1 '2
\ [2]  [1]8  '2     % Chace: [2 1]8, only the 8 survives; Peet: \ '18  '2 ("The papyrus is damaged, but the reading certain")

2 ÷ 11
{'6}  1 2/3 '6
{'66}  '6
[1]     [11]        % Chace: the whole of this column is restored ("[1 ... 1 2/3 '6]"); the plate shows nothing of it
[2/3]   [7 '3]
['3]    [3 2/3]
\ ['6]  [1 2/3 '6]  % the tick is inside Chace's restoration too
[1]  11             % Peet: [1  1]1
[2]  [2]2
[4]  [4]4
\ 6  66  6          % Chace: the third number is written without the dot ("there may have been a dot on the papyrus, obscured now by a crack or fold"); Peet: [6]6 (the first 6 of 66 restored) and '6

2 ÷ 13
{'8}  1 '2 '8
{'52}  '4
{'104}  '8
  1    1[3]         % Peet: 13, unbracketed
  '2   6 '2
  '4   3 '4
\ '8   1 '2 '8
\ 4    '52   '4
\ 8    '104  '8

2 ÷ 15
{'10}  1 '2
{'30}  '2
  1     15
\ '10   1 '2
\ '30   '2

2 ÷ 17
{"Call 2"} "out of 17"
{'12}  1 '3 '12
{'51}  '3
{'68}  '4
{"Working out:"}
  1    17
  2/3  11 '3
  '3   5 2/3
  6    2 '2 '3      % Chace: "This number should be '6 and not 6"; Peet: '6 (dots corrected silently)
\ '12  1 '4 '6
Remainder '3 '4.    % ticked in the papyrus: "\ ḏꜣ·t '3 '4", Remainder (2 less 1 '3 '12)
  1    '17          % Chace: the middle numbers are dotted here (17 and 34 also); a double statement, not a column of '17
  2    '34
\ 3    '51   '3
\ 4    '68   '4

2 ÷ 19
{'12}  1 '2 '12
{'76}  '4           % Chace: "The dot before the red fraction '76 ... seems to have been made in black and then corrected to red"
{'114}  '6
  1    19           % no row of this column is ticked, in Chace or Peet
  2/3  12 2/3
  '3   6 '3
  '6   3 '6
  '12  1 '2 '12
Remainder '4 '6.    % ḏꜣ·t
  1    '19          % Peet: 19, 38, 76 without dots
  2    '38
\ 4    '76   '4
Remainder '6.       % ḏꜣ·t
  1    '19
  2    '38
  4    76           % Chace: "the 76 is written without a dot although the first two partial products are dotted"
"Total"             % dmd, written in the papyrus on the same line as the next row, before its tick; Peet omits it
\ 6    '114  '6     % Peet: \ 6  114  '6

2 ÷ 21
{'14}  1 '2
{42}  '2            % Chace: "The fractional dot is omitted in the second term of the answer"; the number is '42
  1     21
\ 2/3   '14  1 '2   % Peet: 14 without the dot
\ 2     42   '2

2 ÷ 23
{'12}  1 2/3 '4
{'276}  '12
  1    23
  2/3  15 '3
  '3   7 2/3
  '6   3 '2 '3
\ '12  1 '2 '4 '6
Remainder '12.      % ḏꜣ·t, not ticked
  1    23
\ 10   230
\ 2    46
"Total"             % dmd, in the multiplier column; the next figures stand on the same line
\ '276  '12         % Chace: the tick stands before '276, in the product column (10 and 2 make 12, 230 and 46 make 276); Peet: "Total '276 '12", no tick

2 ÷ 25
{'15}  1 2/3
{'75}  '3
  1     25
\ '15   1 2/3
\ 3     '75  '3

2 ÷ 27
{'18}  1 '2
{'54}  '2
  1     27
\ 2/3   '18  1 '2
\ 2     '54  '2

2 ÷ 29
{"Call 2"} "out of 29"
{'24}  1 '6 '24
{'58}  '2
{'174}  '6
{'232}  '8
{"Working-out:"}
\ 1    '24   1 '6 '24   % Chace: "The scribe has been careless here ... it was natural to put '1' at the beginning of the first line"; Peet: "1 (sic)", "obviously an error"; Peet also prints a first row "1  29" which Chace does not have
\ 2    '58   '2
\ 6    174   '6         % Chace: 174 without the dot; Peet: '174
\ 8    '232  '8

2 ÷ 31
"31"                % the divisor, in black at the head of the entry; Peet prints it as the row "1  31"
{'20}  1 '2 '20
{'124}  '4
{'155}  '5
  1    '20   1 '2 '20   % Chace: "the scribe has by mistake put '1' at the top of the first column, opposite '20"; Peet: "1 (sic)", "The dot 1 in front of '20 is an error"
\ 4    124   '4         % Chace: 124 without the dot; Peet: '124
\ 5    '155  '5

2 ÷ 33
"33"                % the divisor, at the head; Peet prints it as the row "1  33"
{'22}  1 '2
{'66}  '2
  2/3  22    1 '2       % not ticked (so also Peet); Chace: 22 without the dot, Peet: '22
\ 2    '66   '2

2 ÷ 35
"35"                % the divisor, at the head; Peet prints it as the row "1  35"
{30}  1 '6          % Chace: the dot is omitted with this 30 on the plate, "possibly ... concealed under the patch"
{42}  2/3 '6        % Chace: dot omitted with the sign for 40, see the note to 2 ÷ 21
{"6"} "7" "5"       % auxiliary figures on the line below: red 6 under the 35, black 7 under '30, black 5 under '42 (the sixths: 1 '6 is 7 sixths, 2/3 '6 is 5 sixths, Peet). Peet reads the 6 as standing at the beginning of the line, not under 35
\ '30  1 '6
\ 42   2/3 '6       % Chace: dot omitted with 42 (note to 2 ÷ 21); Peet: '42

2 ÷ 37
{'24}  1 '2 '24     % Chace prints a small stroke above and below the '2; read as '2 (so Peet)
{'111}  '3
{'296}  '8
  1    37
  2/3  24 2/3
  '3   12 '3
  '6   6 '6
  '12  3 '12
\ '24  1 '2 '24
Remainder '3 '8.    % ḏꜣ·t; Chace prints a small stroke above the '3 and below; read as '3 (so Peet)
  1    37
  2    74
\ 3    '111  '3
Remainder '8.       % ḏꜣ·t
  1    37
  2    74
  4    148
\ 8    296   '8

2 ÷ 39
"39"                % the divisor, at the head; Peet prints it as the row "1  39"
{'26}  1 '2
{'78}  '2
\ 2/3  26    1 '2   % Chace: 26 without the dot; Peet: '26
  2    78    '2     % not ticked (so also Peet); Chace: 78 without the dot; Peet: '78

2 ÷ 41
{"Call 2"} "out of 41"
{'24}  1 2/3 '24
{'246}  '6
{'328}  '8
{"Working-out:"}
  2/3  '27 '3       % Chace: "The scribe has carelessly added a fractional dot to the 27"; Peet: 27 '3, and Peet prints a first row "1  41" which Chace does not have
  '3   13 2/3
  '6   6 2/3 '6
  '12  3 '3 '12
\ '24  1 2/3 '24
Remainder '6 '8.    % ḏꜣ·t
  1    41
\ 2    82
\ 4    164
"Total"             % dmd, on the same line as the next row, before its tick (so also Peet)
\ 6    '246  '6
\ 8    '328  '8

2 ÷ 43
"43"                % the divisor, at the head; Peet prints it as the row "1  43"
{42}  1 42          % Chace: both without the dot (the sign for 40, see the note to 2 ÷ 21); the numbers are '42
{'66}  '2           % Chace: "The sign for 60 is used here twice in what was intended to be '86"; Peet: '86, without comment
{'129}  '3
{'301}  '7
"Find"              % gm, written in the multiplier column of the next row
\ 42   1 '42        % Chace: the tick stands before the 42, in the middle column; Peet: "Found \ '42  1 '42"
\ 2    '66   '2     % Chace: 60 for 80 again, intended '86; Peet: '86
  3    '129  '3     % not ticked (so also Peet)
\ 7    '301  '7

2 ÷ 45
"45"                % the divisor, at the head; Peet prints it as the row "1  45"
{'30}  1 '2
{'90}  '2
\ 2/3  30    1 '2   % Chace: 30 without the dot; Peet: '30
\ 2    '90   '2

2 ÷ 47
"47"                % the divisor, at the head; Peet prints it as the row "1  47"
{'30}  1 '2 '15
{'141}  '3
{'470}  '10
"Find"              % gm, in the multiplier column of the next row
'30    1 '2 '15     % not ticked (so also Peet)
\ 3    '141  '3
\ 10   '470  '10

2 ÷ 49
"49"                % the divisor, at the head; Peet prints it as the row "1  49"
{'28}  1 '2 '4
{'196}  '4
"Find"              % gm, in the multiplier column of the next row
'28    1 '2 '4      % not ticked (so also Peet)
\ 4    '196  '4
about: Table of 2 divided by the odd numbers, entries 2 ÷ 3 to 2 ÷ 49. Chace vol. II pl. 2-15 (photographs I-IV), PDF pp. 51-78; Peet pp. 38-43 (Pl. A-B), summary table p. 37.

name: table-2n-b
label: 2 ÷ 51 to 2 ÷ 101
text:
% Table of 2 divided by the odd numbers, entries 2 ÷ 51 to 2 ÷ 101. Chace vol. II pls. 15-33, PDF pp. 77-114 (literal translation on the odd page, plate on the even); Peet pp. 43-47 (Pls. B, C, D).
% Read from page images by a coding agent's sub-agent; no person checked it. See sources/notes/table-2n-b.md.
%
% Layout, as Chace prints it. Each entry opens with the divisor standing alone, in black (written as a quoted line, "57"; Peet renders it as a row "1 57"),
% or with a "Call 2 out of n" heading,
% then the answer: each red part of n followed by what it gives, one pair to a row ({'30}  1 2/3 '10 = "'30 of 53 is 1 2/3 '10").
% Then the working-out. A row of two figures is a part of n and what it gives. A row of three figures is the
% scribe's side reckoning: the multiplier k written at the left (ticked), then k times n (the part 1/(kn) when
% dotted), then the part of n it gives (\ 6  '318  '6 = "6 times 53 is 318; '318 of 53 is '6").
% Dots are kept as Chace prints them. Chace (note to 2 ÷ 17): "in most of the multiplications carried through for
% the purpose of obtaining fractional multipliers ... the partial products are written without dots", so a figure
% written here without the part sign (34, 102, 536, ...) is the papyrus's bare number, not a correction.
% Peet's answer lines are prose ("1 '2 is '34th") and his columns start with a "1 n" row of his own; neither is
% compared figure by figure here except where the value or a restoration differs. Dot differences in the working are noted
% ("% Peet: '40"), but Peet says (p. 38) that "the incorrect omission or insertion of the fractional dot ... has been
% corrected without further comment in these division sums", so they are Peet's normalisations, not other readings.

2 ÷ 51
% Chace PDF p. 77 (pl. 15, p. 78); Peet p. 43 (Pl. B)
"51"
{'34}   1 '2
{'102}  ['2]      % Peet: <'2>, "never stood in the papyrus", omitted by the scribe (Peet's pointed brackets); Chace restores it as damage
\ 2/3   34    1 '2
\ 2     102   '2

2 ÷ 53
% Chace PDF p. 79 (pl. 16, p. 80); Peet p. 43 (Pl. B)
{"Call 2"}
"out of 53"
{'30}   1 2/3 '10
{'318}  '6
{'795}  '15
{"Working-out:"}
"Find"            % Peet: "There is a dot (= multiplier 1) after 'found' which should not be there. Cf. 2 ÷ 29 and 2 ÷ 31."
\ 30    1 2/3 '10      % Chace prints 30 without the dot (see note to 2 ÷ 17); Peet: '30
\ 6     '318  '6
Remainder '15.
  1     '53       % Chace: "In this multiplication we should expect dots with all the numbers of the second column, or with only the last, or not at all"; Peet: 53
\ 10    530
\ 5     265
"Total"
  15    '795  '15

2 ÷ 55
% Chace PDF p. 79 (pl. 16, p. 80); Peet p. 44 (Pl. B)
"55"
{'30}   1 2/3 '6
{'330}  '6
"Find"
\ '30   1 2/3 '6
\ 6     '330  '6

2 ÷ 57
% Chace PDF p. 81 (pl. 17, p. 82); Peet p. 44 (Pl. C)
"57"
{38}    1 '2      % Chace: "Fractional dot omitted." (for '38)
{'114}  '2
\ 2/3   38    1 '2
\ 2     114   '2

2 ÷ 59
% Chace PDF p. 81 (pl. 17, p. 82); Peet p. 44 (Pl. C)
"59"
{'36}   1 '2 '12 '18
{'226}  '4        % so in Chace's translation and plate (red 226; the working has 236); no comment by Chace; Peet: '236
{'531}  '9
"Find"
\ '36   1 '2 '12 '18
\ 4     '236  '4
\ 9     531   '9       % Peet: '531

2 ÷ 61
% Chace PDF p. 83 (pl. 18, p. 84); Peet p. 44 (Pl. C)
"61"
{'40}   1 '2 '40
{'244}  '4
{'488}  '8
{'610}  '10
"Find"
\ 40    1 '2 '40       % Chace prints 40 without the dot; Peet: '40
\ 4     '244  '4
\ 8     '488  '8
\ 10    '610  '10

2 ÷ 63
% Chace PDF p. 85 (pl. 19, p. 86); Peet p. 44 (Pl. C)
"63"
{42}    1 '2      % Chace: see note to 2 ÷ 21 (the fractional dot is omitted with the sign for 40)
{'126}  '2
\ 2/3   42    1 '2     % Peet: '42
\ 2     '126  '2

2 ÷ 65
% Chace PDF p. 87 (pl. 20, p. 88); Peet p. 44 (Pl. C)
{"Call 2"}
"out of 65"
{'39}   1 2/3
{'195}  '3
{"Working-out:"}
"Find"
  '39   1 2/3          % no tick (so both editions)
\ 3     '195  '3

2 ÷ 67
% Chace PDF p. 89 (pl. 21, p. 90); Peet p. 44 (Pl. C)
"67"
{40}    1 '2 '8 '20      % Chace: see note to 2 ÷ 21 (fractional dot omitted with the sign for 40)
{'335}  '5
{'536}  '8
"Find"
\ 40    1 '2 '8 '20      % Chace prints 40 without the dot; Peet: '40
\ 5     '335  '5
\ 8     536   '8         % Peet: '536

2 ÷ 69
% Chace PDF p. 89 (pl. 21, p. 90); Peet p. 45 (Pl. C)
"69"
{46}    1 '2      % Chace: see note to 2 ÷ 21
{'138}  '2
\ 2/3   46    1 '2     % Peet: '46
\ 2     138   '2       % Peet: '138

2 ÷ 71
% Chace PDF p. 91 (pl. 22, p. 92); Peet p. 45 (Pl. C)
"71"
{40}    1 '2 '4 '40      % Chace: see note to 2 ÷ 21
{'568}  '8
{'710}  '10
"Find"
  '40   1 '2 '4 '40      % no tick (so both editions)
\ 8     568   '8         % Peet: '568
\ 10    710   '10        % Peet: '710

2 ÷ 73
% Chace PDF p. 93 (pl. 23, p. 94); Peet p. 45 (Pl. C)
"73"
{'60}   1 '6 '20
{'219}  '3
{'292}  '4
{'365}  '5
"Find"
\ '60   1 '6 '20
\ 3     '219  '3
\ 4     '292  '4
\ 5     365   5          % Chace: "Photograph VI seems to show a crease or overlap in the papyrus here. It is possible that a fractional dot, now concealed, was written over this 5."; Peet: '365, '5

2 ÷ 75
% Chace PDF p. 95 (pl. 24, p. 96); Peet p. 45 (Pl. C)
"75"
{'50}   1 '2
{'150}  '2
\ 2/3   50    1 '2     % Peet: '50
\ 2     '150  '2

2 ÷ 77
% Chace PDF p. 97 (pl. 25, p. 98); Peet p. 45 (Pl. C)
{"Call 2"}
"out of 77"
{'44}   1 '2 '4
{'308}  '4
{"Working-out:"}
"Find"
  '44   1 '2 '4          % no tick; Peet: '4[4] (second 4 restored)
\ 4     '3[08]  '4

2 ÷ 79
% Chace PDF p. 99 (pl. 26, p. 100); Peet p. 45 (Pl. C)
"79"
{'60}   1 '4 '15
{'237}  '3
{'316}  '4
{'790}  '10
"Find"
\ '60   1 '4 '15
\ 3     '233  '3       % Chace: "These numbers should be 237 and 316 as in the line at the top."; Peet: "In the working read '237 and '316."
\ 4     '416  '4       % Chace: "should be ... 316"; Peet: "read ... '316"
\ 10    '790  '10

2 ÷ 81
% Chace PDF p. 101 (pl. 27, p. 102); Peet p. 45 (Pl. C)
"81"
{54}    1 '2      % Chace: "Fractional dot omitted."
{'162}  '2
\ 2/3   '54   1 '2
\ 2     162   '2       % Peet: '162

2 ÷ 83
% Chace PDF p. 103 (pl. 28, p. 104); Peet p. 46 (Pl. C)
"63"                % Chace: "63 was written for 83. See note to 2 divided by 43."; Peet: 83 (in his "1 83" row; no remark)
{['60]}  1 '3 '20      % red '60 restored (so both editions)
{'332}  '4
{'415}  '5
{'498}  '6
"Find"
\ '60   1 '3 '20
\ 4     332   '4       % Peet: '332
\ 5     '415  '5
\ 6     '498  '6

2 ÷ 85
% Chace PDF p. 105 (pl. 29, p. 106); Peet p. 46 (Pl. C)
"'85"               % Chace prints 85 with a dot over it (the plate's gloss is dotted too), without comment; Peet: 85
{'51}   1 2/3
{'255}  '3
  1     85
"Find"
\ 51    1 2/3          % Peet: '51
\ 3     255   '3       % Peet: '255

2 ÷ 87
% Chace PDF p. 105 (pl. 29, p. 106); Peet p. 46 (Pl. D)
  1     87
{58}    1 '2      % Chace: "Fractional dot omitted."
{'174}  '2
\ 2/3   58    [1] '2   % 1 restored (so both editions); Peet: '58
\ 2     '174  '2

2 ÷ 89
% Chace PDF p. 107 (pl. 30, p. 108); Peet p. 46 (Pl. D)
{"Call 2"}
"out of 89"
{'60}   [1 '3] '10 '20     % Peet: [1 '3] '10 '20, the same
{'356}  ['4]               % Chace: "An error has crept into Peet's Plate D, where '336 occurs in his hieroglyphic transcription." (Peet's text has '356)
{['53]4}  '6               % red '534 with '53 restored (Chace prints a black dot before it, inside the restoration); the red 4 and the black '6 are from the New York fragments (Chace n. 2); Peet: '[53]4, '6
{'890}  ['10]              % red '890 from the New York fragments: "the fractional dot and part of the 90" survive (Chace n. 2); Peet: '890, ['10]
{"Working-out:"}
"Find"
  60    1 '3 '10 '20       % no tick (so both editions); Chace prints 60 without the dot; Peet: '60
\ 4     '356  '4
\ 6     '534  '6
\ 10    '890  '10

2 ÷ 91
% Chace PDF p. 107 (pl. 30, p. 108); Peet p. 46 (Pl. D)
"91"
{'70}   1 '5 '10
{'130}  2/3 30     % Chace: "Fractional dot omitted." (30 for '30)
"Find"
  '70   1 '5 '10       % no tick in Chace; Peet: ticked
"Find"
  '130  2/3 30         % Chace: "Fractional dot omitted."; Peet: 2/3 '30; Peet: "The working is little more than a restatement of the answer."

2 ÷ 93
% Chace PDF p. 109 (pl. 31, p. 110); Peet p. 46 (Pl. D)
"[9]3"              % Peet: 93, not marked restored (in his "1 93" row)
{'62}   1 '2
{'166}  '2        % Chace: "166 was written for 186. See note to 2 divided by 43."; Peet: '186, no remark
"Find"
\ '62   1 '2
\ 2     166   '2       % Chace: "166 was written for 186."; Peet: '186, no remark

2 ÷ 95
% Chace PDF p. 109 (pl. 31, p. 110); Peet p. 46 (Pl. D)
"95"
{'60}   1 '2 ['12]     % Peet: 1 '2 '12, '12 not marked restored
{380}   ['4]           % Chace: "The fractional dot may have existed on a missing fragment of papyrus."; Peet: '380, ['4]
{'570}  '6             % Chace: '570 on a fragment now misplaced in register 3 (Chace n. 3); '6 on a New York fragment Chace places here (n. 4); Peet restores both: ['6 is '570]
"Find"
  60    1 '2 '12       % no tick (so both editions); Chace prints 60 without the dot; Peet: '60
\ 4     '380  '4
\ 6     '570  '6

2 ÷ 97
% Chace PDF p. 111 (pl. 32, p. 112); Peet p. 47 (Pl. D)
"97"
{'56}   1 '2 '8 '14 '28
{'679}  '7             % Chace: "The 9 and the portions of figures that follow are on the New York fragments. The 670 is on a fragment that is incorrectly placed at the edge of B. M. 10058, in register 4"
{'77[6]}  ['8]         % so both editions (Peet: '77[6], ['8])
"Find"
\ 56    1 '2 '8 '14 '28     % Chace prints 56 without the dot; Peet: '56
\ 7     679   '7       % Peet: '679
\ 8     776   '8       % Peet: '776

2 ÷ 99
% Chace PDF p. 111 (pl. 32, p. 112); Peet p. 47 (Pl. D)
"99"
{'66}   1 '2
{'198}  '2        % Chace: three New York fragments placed in '198 "practically completing it", and another completing the following '2
"Find"
\ 2/3   66    1 '2     % Peet: '66
  2     198   '2       % no tick (so both editions); Peet: '198

2 ÷ 101
% Chace PDF p. 113 (pl. 33, p. 114); Peet p. 47 (Pl. D). Chace: "The surviving portions of this example and table ... are all from the New York fragments."
{"[Call 2]"}           % Chace n. 1: a stroke in black ink at the top of the fragment, "perhaps a low-placed dot between nys and 2 ... or possibly a stroke of the 2, although the 2 is everywhere red in these headings except in 2 divided by 3"

name: no-41

% Problem 41. Chace vol. II pl. 63 (photograph XVIII), PDF pp. 173-174; Peet pp. 80-81 (Pl. M).

name: no-42
label: No. 42
text:
% Problem 42. Chace vol. II pl. 64 (photographs XVIII-XIX), PDF pp. 175-176; Peet pp. 81-82 (Pl. N).
No. 42
{"A granary round,"} "of 10 by 10."
"Take away thou '9 of 10, namely 1 '9; the remainder is: 8 2/3 '6 '18."

"Manner of the reckoning of it."
  1     8 2/3 '6 '18

  4     35 '2 '18
\ 8     71 '9

  '3    2 2/3 '6 '12 36 '54   % Chace n.3: scribe omitted the fraction dot on the 36

name: no-43
label: No. 43
text:
% Problem 43. Chace vol. II pl. 65, PDF pp. 177-178; Peet pp. 82-85 (Pl. N).
No. 43
{"A granary round of"} "cubit 9 in the height of it, 6 in the breadth of it; what is that which goes into it in grain?"   % Chace: "In the statement of the problem the given dimensions are transposed"; Peet: statement incorrect, 9 is really the diameter and 6 the height
"The doing as it occurs:"
"Take away thou 1 from 9; the remainder is 8."
"Operate on 8, make thou '3 of it to it; becomes it:" {"10 2/3."}
"Multiply: 10 2/3 times 10 2/3; becomes it: 113 2/3 '9."   % Chace n.2: the scribe first omitted the word tp (multiply) and later inserted it above the line
"Make the multiplication: 113 2/3 '9 up to times 4; 2/3, this is, of the cubit 6, which is: the breadth; becomes it: 455 '9;" {"the content of it, this is, in khar."}
"Find thou '20 of the content of it in khar; becomes it: 22 '2 '4 '45;"   % Chace n.4: "This should be '180"; Peet: (sic), read '180
"what goes, this is, into it (in grain hekat) in quadruple hekat:" {"grain, 2200 hekat 50 25 '2 '32 '64 2 ro '2 '4 '36."}   % Chace n.5: the words in parenthesis "crept in through an error of the ancient copyist"; Peet: "clearly a scribe's error and to be omitted"
"Manner of working out:"
\ 1     8
  2/3   5 '3
\ '3    2 2/3
Total 10 2/3.
  1     10 2/3
\ 10    106 2/3
\ 2/3   7 '9

  2     227 '2 '18

name: no-44
label: No. 44
text:
% Problem 44. Chace vol. II pl. 66 (photographs XIX-XX), PDF pp. 179-180; Peet pp. 84-85 (Pl. N).
No. 44
{"Example of reckoning"} "a granary four-angled, (of 10 in) the length of it 10, the breadth of it 10, the height of it 10; what is that which goes into it in grain?"   % Chace n.3 and Peet: the scribe confused two ways of stating it; the words "of 10 in" are surplus (Peet: delete them, or else insert m twice and delete the fourth 10)
"Multiply: 10 times 10; becomes it: 100."
"Multiply: 100 times 10; becomes it: 1000."
"Make thou '2 of 1000, namely, 500; becomes it: 1500; the content of it, this is, in khar."
"Make thou '20 of 1500; becomes it: 75; what goes, this is, into it in quadruple hekat;" {"grain, (hekat) 7500 hekat."}   % Chace n.5: the first "hekat" is redundant
"Example of working out:"
% the papyrus also draws a square with 10 in it and 10 beside it (Peet p. 84; the hieratic on Chace pl. 66); the notation has no figure
  1     10
  10    100
  1     100
  10    1000
  1     1000
  '2    500
  1     1500
  '10   150
  '20   75
  1     75
  10    750       % Chace n.6: "The scribe seems inadvertently to have put here what looks like a fractional dot"
\ 20    1500
  '10   150       % '10 of 1500
"'10 of '10: 15."            % a row of the column above ('10 of '10 of 1500); the notation's multiplier cannot hold "'10 of '10"
"2/3 of '10 of '10 of it: 10."   % likewise; Peet: these three lines are "a proof by continued division, if indeed they have not merely strayed hither from No. 45"

name: no-45
label: No. 45
text:
% Problem 45. Chace vol. II pl. 67, PDF pp. 181-182; Peet p. 85 (Pl. N).
No. 45
{"A granary,"} "has gone grain into it in quadruple hekat 75[00 hekat]. Of, it is, how much by how much?"   % Chace n.1: "The scribe, as Peet indicates, forgot to write the hekat-sign after the number 75"; Peet: "75 (hundreds of) quadruple-hekat"
"Make thou the multiplication: 75 up to times 20; becomes it: 1500."
"Make thou the operation on 1500, make thou '10 of it, namely, 150; '10 of '10 of it, 15; 2/3 of '10 of '10 of it, namely, 10."
"Therefore of, it is, 10 by 10 by 10."
  1     75
  10    750
  20    1500
"Behold the content of it this is."
  1     1500
  '10   150
"'10 of '10 of it: 15."            % a row of the column; the notation's multiplier cannot hold "'10 of '10"
"2/3 of '10 of '10 of it: 10."
about: Problem 45. Chace vol. II pl. 67, PDF pp. 181-182; Peet p. 85 (Pl. N).

name: no-46
label: No. 46
text:
% Problem 46. Chace vol. II pl. 68, PDF pp. 183-184; Peet p. 87 (Pl. N).
No. 46
{"A granary,"} "has gone grain into it in quadruple hekat" {"2500 hekat."} "What are the dimensions of it?"
"Make thou the multiplication: 25 up to times 20; becomes it: 500; the content of it this is."
"Make thou the operation on 500; make thou '10 of it, namely, 50; '20 of it, namely, 25; '10 of '10 of it, namely, 5; 2/3 of '10 of '10 of it, namely, 3 '3; of, it is, 10 by 10 by 3 '3, the granary."

  1     25

"The content of it this is."
  1     500
  '10   50
"'10 of '10 of it: 5."             % a row of the column; the notation's multiplier cannot hold "'10 of '10"
"2/3 of '10 of '10 of it: 3 '3."
"Becomes granary this, in cubit, 10 by 10 by 3 '3; the same this is."
about: Problem 46. Chace vol. II pl. 68, PDF pp. 183-184; Peet p. 87 (Pl. N).
words: Make thou the multiplication: 25 up to times 20; becomes it: 500; the content of it this is.

name: no-47
label: No. 47
text:
% Problem 47. Chace vol. II pl. 69 (photographs XIX-XX), PDF pp. 185-186; Peet pp. 87-88 (Pl. O).
No. 47
{"If says to thee the scribe,"} "Cause thou that know I '10, when becomes it: a rectangular granary, a circular granary or."   % Chace n.2: the clause "when becomes it" is unnecessary (Griffith); Peet restores "Let me know <what> '10 becomes", supposing words lost by haplography
"'10 is to be: grain, quadruple hekat 10"
% A table of the parts of 100 quadruple hekat. "hekat" and "ro" here are quadruple hekat and quadruple ro (Peet p. 88); a ro is 1/320 of the hekat.
% Each row: the part, then what it is "to be" (written "ditto" in the papyrus after the first).
  '10    10 hekat
  '20    5 hekat
  '30    3 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro       % written "ro 2/3": ro alone stands for 1 ro (Chace)
  '40    2 '2 hekat
  '50    2 hekat
  '60    1 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro
  '70    1 '4 '8 '32 '64 hekat 2 '14 '21 '42 ro
  '80    1 '4 hekat
  '90    1 '16 '32 '64 hekat '2 '18 ro     % the word ro is not written where there are only fractions of a ro (Chace); Chace prints a small mark over the '2 here, not explained
  '100   1 hekat
about: Problem 47. Chace vol. II pl. 69 (photographs XIX-XX), PDF pp. 185-186; Peet pp. 87-88 (Pl. O).

name: no-48
label: No. 48
text:
% Problem 48. Chace vol. II pl. 70 (photograph XIX), PDF pp. 187-188; Peet pp. 88-89 (Pl. O).
No. 48
% No words. A figure: a square with a circle (drawn as an octagon) inside it, and 9 written in the circle. The notation has no figure.
% The papyrus writes areas over 10 setat as a number of "thousands-of-land" (each 10 setat) before the word setat, then the remaining setat:

  1     8 setat

  4     32 setat      % written 3 (thousands-of-land) 2 setat

  2     18 setat      % written 1 (thousand-of-land) 8 setat
  4     36 setat      % written 3 (thousands-of-land) 6 setat; Chace n.1: special sign for 6; Peet n.3: "The text has 60 setat"
\ 8     72 setat      % written 7 (thousands-of-land) 2 setat
Total 81 setat.       % written 8 (thousands-of-land) 1 setat

name: no-49

text:
% Problem 49. Chace vol. II pl. 71 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 189-190; Peet pp. 89-90 (Pl. O).
No. 49
{"Example of reckoning area."} "If is said to thee, A rectangle of land, of khet 10 by khet 2, what is the area of it?"   % Chace n.4: "The solution is for 1 khet instead of 2"; Peet: "If we read 1 khet instead of 2 for the shorter side the working will be correct"

"The doing as it occurs:"
  1     1000

text:
% Problem 50. Chace vol. II pl. 72 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 191-192; Peet p. 90 (Pl. O).
No. 50
{"Example of making"} "a field round of khet 9. What is the amount of it in area?"
"Take away thou '9 of it, namely, 1; the remainder is: 8."

"The doing as it occurs:"
  1     9

"Take away from it; the remainder is 8."
  1     8
  2     16
  4     32
\ 8     64

name: no-51
label: No. 51
text:
% Problem 51. Chace vol. II pl. 73 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 193-194; Peet pp. 91-94 (Pl. O).
No. 51
{"Example of making a triangle in land."} "If is said to thee, A triangle of khet 10 on the side of it, khet 4 in the base of it, what is the area of it?"
% The papyrus draws a long triangle, 10 khet written along its upper side and 4 khet beside its short base (Chace pl. 73; Peet p. 91). The notation has no figure.
"The doing as it occurs:"     % Peet sets "You are to take half of 4 ... This is its acreage" (below) here, before the working; Chace sets it after
  1     400
  '2    200
  1     1000
  2     2000
"The area of it this is: 2."  % Chace translates "20 setat" (2 thousands-of-land); Peet: "Its acreage is 2", sc. thousands-of-land
"Make thou '2 of 4, namely, 2, for the giving of the rectangle of it."
"Make thou the multiplication: 10 up to times 2; the area of it this is."
about: Problem 51. Chace vol. II pl. 73 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 193-194; Peet pp. 91-94 (Pl. O).

name: no-52
label: No. 52
text:
% Problem 52. Chace vol. II pl. 74 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 195-196; Peet pp. 94-95 (Pl. P).
No. 52
{"Example of making a cut-off triangle of land."} "If is said to thee, A cut-off triangle of land of (n.t) khet 20 on the side of it, khet 6 in the base of it, khet 4 on the cut-off; what is the area of it?"   % Chace n.2: "The scribe has repeated the word n.t by mistake"
% The papyrus draws a trapezoid, 20 khet along its long side, 6 khet at one end and 4 khet at the other (Chace pl. 74). The notation has no figure.
"Add thou the base of it to the cut-off; there become 10."
"Make thou '2 of 10, namely, 5, for the giving of the rectangle of it."
"Make thou the multiplication: 20 up to times 5; there become 10; the area of it this is."   % Peet: "result 10 (sic)"; Chace n.5: 100 setat, "which the Egyptian would write simply 10"
"The doing as it occurs:"
  1     1000
  '2    500
\ 1     2000
  2     4000
\ 4     8000
Total 10000.
"making in area 20; the amount of it, this is, in area."   % papyrus writes 20 (Chace translates "200 setat"); Chace n.5: "The answer should be 100 setat, which the Egyptian would write simply 10 ... by mistake he wrote 20 instead of 10"; Peet: "20 (read 10)"
about: Problem 52. Chace vol. II pl. 74 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 195-196; Peet pp. 94-95 (Pl. P).
words: Add thou the base of it to the cut-off; there become 10.

name: no-53
label: No. 53
text:
% Problem 53. Chace vol. II pl. 75 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 197-198; Peet pp. 95-96 (Pl. P).
No. 53
% No statement of the problem. A figure: a long triangle divided into three parts by two lines across it, with numbers in red
% (Peet: the base of the apex part marked 2 '4 in red, its area 7 '2 '4 '8 in red, and a 7 along the lower side near the apex). The notation has no figure.
% Chace: "For explanation and statement of numerical mistakes, see volume 1, page 94." Peet: "a problem which is clearly incomplete and incorrect".
% Fractions of the setat are written with the special setat signs (Chace; Peet pp. 24-5).
\ 1     4 '2 setat
\ 2     9 setat
  '2    2 '4 setat     % Chace n.1: "The scribe has here by mistake written the multiplier '2 in the special notation for '2 setat"; Peet likewise
  '4    1 '8 setat     % Peet: ticked
{Total} 5 '2 '8 setat.  % "Total" (dmd) in red. 5 '2 '8 is the 1 and '4 rows (4 '2 times 1 '4); Peet: correct "despite inaccurate ticking and the introduction of an unnecessary step"
"'10 of it: 1 '4 '8 setat, cubit-strip 10."   % Chace n.2: cubit-strip 10 is written with a sign exactly like 30 (Peet: a special sign for 10 cubits-of-land; Griffith and Moeller suspected a mistake); Peet: these lines "are totally unconnected with this, and clearly come from some other reckoning"
"'10 of it is: to be taken away; then this is: the amount."
  1     7 setat
\ 2     14 setat       % written 1 (thousand-of-land) 4 setat
  '2    3 '2 setat     % Chace n.1: the multiplier '2 written in the special notation for '2 setat
\ '4    1 '2 '4 setat
{Total} 15 '2 '4 setat.  % "Total" in red. Written "setat 1 5 '2 '4": Chace n.4: "This should be 1 setat 5, etc. The setat sign is placed over the 1 instead of the 5 by mistake"; Peet: "1 thousand-of-land and (5 '2 '4) setat"
\ '2    7 '2 '4 '8 setat   % half of the total 15 '2 '4, not of 7; Peet: no tick here
about: Problem 53. Chace vol. II pl. 75 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 197-198; Peet pp. 95-96 (Pl. P).
words: '10 of it: 1 '4 '8 setat, cubit-strip 10.

{"The taking away"} "of the area [setat 7] from fields 10."   % Chace n.1: "setat 7" "Omitted by the scribe"; Peet: "<7 setat>", "unfortunately omitted by the scribe"

\ '2    5
\ '5    2

\ 2     1 '4 '8 setat 2 '2 cubit

name: no-55
label: No. 55
text:
% Problem 55. Chace vol. II pl. 77 (photographs XX-XXI), PDF pp. 201-202; Peet pp. 96-97 (Pl. P).
No. 55
{"The taking away"} "of the area setat 3 from fields, setat 1."   % Chace n.1: "This should have been simply the number 5 instead of setat 1"; Peet: the scribe "has written '1 setat' instead of the simple numeral 5, which it remotely resembles"
Reckon with 5 to find 3.   % papyrus: "Make thou the operation on setat 5 for the finding of the area setat 3."; Peet: "5 setat (sic)"

name: no-56
label: No. 56
text:
% Problem 56. Chace vol. II pl. 78 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 203-204; Peet pp. 97-98 (Pl. Q).
No. 56
{"Example of reckoning"} "a pyramid; 360 in the ukha-thebet, 250 in the per-em-us to it therein; cause thou that know I the seked of it."
% The papyrus draws a pyramid, 250 written beside it and 360 below it (Chace pl. 78). The notation has no figure.
"Make thou '2 of 360; becomes it: 180."
"Make thou the operation on 250 for the finding of 180; there becomes '2 '5 '50 of a cubit."   % the working of this division is not written
"Is cubit this: palm 7."
"Make thou the operation on 7."
  1     7
  '2    3 '2
  5     1 '3 '15     % Chace n.4: "Fractional dot omitted" on the multiplier 5
  '50   '10 '25
"The seked of it is palm 5 '25."   % the s of "seked" (skd) is red in Chace

name: no-57
label: No. 57
text:
% Problem 57. Chace vol. II pl. 79 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 205-206; Peet p. 99 (Pl. Q).
No. 57
{"A pyramid,"} "140 in the ukha-thebet, palm 5 finger 1 in the seked of it. What is the per-em-us to it therein?"
% The papyrus draws a pyramid with 93 '3 beside it and 140 below it (Chace pl. 79). The notation has no figure.
"State thou a cubit in relation to the seked times 2; there become 10 '2."
"Make thou the operation on 10 '2 for the finding of 7; behold a cubit this is."
"Operate on 10 '2: 2/3 of 10 '2 is: 7."
"Make thou the operation on 140; that this is: the ukha-thebet."   % Chace n.2: "The scribe first omitted pw and then added it above the line"
"Make 2/3 of 140, namely, 93 '3; behold the per-em-us, this is, to it therein."
% No columns of working are written; Peet: "The working, though correct ..."
about: Problem 57. Chace vol. II pl. 79 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 205-206; Peet p. 99 (Pl. Q).

name: no-58
label: No. 58
text:
% Problem 58. Chace vol. II pl. 80 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 207-208; Peet p. 99 (Pl. Q).
No. 58
{"A pyramid,"} "the per-em-us to it therein is: 93 '3; cause thou that know I the seked of it; there are 140 in the ukha-thebet."
% The papyrus draws a pyramid with 93 '3 beside it and 140 below it (Chace pl. 80). The notation has no figure.
"Make thou '2 of 140, namely, 70."
Reckon with 93 '3 to find 70.   % papyrus: "Make thou the operation on 93 '3 for the finding of 70."
"Operate on 93 '3, '2 of it is 46 2/3, '4 of it is 23 '3."
"Make thou '2 '4 of a cubit. Operate on 7; '2 of it is 3 '2, '4 of it is 1 '2 '4, the total is palm 5 finger 1; that this is: the seked to it therein."
"Working out:"
  1     93 '3
\ '2    46 2/3
\ '4    23 '3
"Make thou '2 '4 of a cubit. As for cubit this, palm 7 [p]w."   % [p]w restored by Chace
  1     7
  '2    3 '2
  '4    1 '4      % Peet: "1 '4 (read 1 '2 '4)"; Chace prints 1 '4 without comment (the text above has 1 '2 '4)
"The total is palm 5 finger 1; the seked this is."   % the column's figures do not sum to 5 '4 (3 '2 + 1 '4 = 4 '2 '4); the text's 1 '2 '4 does
about: Problem 58. Chace vol. II pl. 80 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 207-208; Peet p. 99 (Pl. Q).

name: no-59
label: No. 59
text:
% Problem 59. Chace vol. II pl. 81 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 209-210; Peet p. 100 (Pl. Q).
No. 59
{"A pyramid,"} "the per-em-us to it therein is: 12, the ukha-thebet to it therein is: 8."   % Chace n.1: "In Problem 59 the given dimensions were transposed"; Peet: "the vertical height (sic) whereof is 12 and the side (sic) 8"; it is the height which must be 8 and the side 12
% The papyrus draws a pyramid with 12 beside it (Chace pl. 81; the figure is shared with No. 59B). The notation has no figure.
Reckon with 8 to find 6.   % papyrus: "Make thou the operation on 8 for the finding of 6; '2, this is, of the per-em-us."
  1     8
\ '2    4
\ '4    2
"Make thou '2 '4 of 7; behold a cubit this is."
  1     7
\ '2    3 '2
\ '4    1 '2 '4
"becomes it: palm 5 finger 2; behold the seked of it this is."   % Chace n.2: the 2 is a "Mistake for 1"; Peet translates "5 palms 1 finger" without comment
"my n m"   % untranslated; Chace n.3: "These signs are difficult to explain" (Gunn: perhaps a corruption of myt.t pw); Peet: "What .....?", "The phrase which ends the problem is a mystery. It may be corrupt."
about: Problem 59. Chace vol. II pl. 81 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 209-210; Peet p. 100 (Pl. Q).
words: Make thou '2 '4 of 7; behold a cubit this is.

name: no-59b
label: No. 59B
text:
% Problem 59B. Chace vol. II pl. 81 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 209-210; Peet p. 100 (Pl. Q).
No. 59B
% Peet: Nos. 59 and 59B are distinct problems; the scribe ran 59B on as part of No. 59's working, opening it with ir.hr.k and without red ink.
"Make thou a pyramid of 12; the seked of it is: palm 5 finger 1; cause thou that know I [the] per-em-us to it therein."   % Chace n.1: "In 59B ... wha-thebet was omitted in connection with 12, perhaps intentionally"; Peet: "a pyramid of 12 (sic)"; Chace restores the [y] of rh.y (Peet: "Let <me> know")
% The figure of No. 59 has 12 written beside it, though here 12 is the side. The notation has no figure.
"Make thou the operation on [palm] 5 finger 1 times 2 for the finding of a cubit; behold palm 7 this is. Becomes it: 10 '2;"   % [palm] restored by Chace; Peet: "which is 7 spans"
"2/3 of it is: 7."
"Make the operation on 12; 2/3 of it is: 4;"   % Chace n.6: "Mistake for 8"; Peet: "4 (read 8)"
"behold the per-em-us this is."
about: Problem 59B. Chace vol. II pl. 81 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 209-210; Peet p. 100 (Pl. Q).
words: Make thou a pyramid of 12; the seked of it is: palm 5 finger 1; cause thou that know I [the] per-em-us to it therein.

name: no-60
label: No. 60
text:
% Problem 60. Chace vol. II pl. 82 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 211-212; Peet pp. 100-102 (Pl. R).
No. 60
{"A pillar (?)"} "of cubit 15 in the sentet of it, 30 in its kay-en-heru; cause thou that know I the seked of it."   % Chace: iwn, "column, pillar, or support"; Peet: "A cone (?)"
% The papyrus draws a plain triangle with 30 beside it and 15 below it (Chace pl. 82). The notation has no figure.
"Operate on 15; '2 of it is: 7 '2."
"Operate on 7 '2 (times 4) for the finding of 30;"   % Chace n.5: "The scribe has by mistake inserted the result in the statement of the operation"; Peet: "Multiply 7 '2 four times (sic) to find 30", "the words spw 4 are not needed"
"becomes the result of it: 4; that this is: the seked to it therein."   % Peet: the scribe divides 30 by 7 '2 where 7 '2 should be divided by 30 ('4 cubit, 1 3/4 palms): "a serious confusion has taken place"
"Working-out:"
  1     15
\ '2    7 '2
  1     7 '2
  2     15
\ 4     30
about: Problem 60. Chace vol. II pl. 82 (photographs XXI-XXII), PDF pp. 211-212; Peet pp. 100-102 (Pl. R).
words: Operate on 15; '2 of it is: 7 '2.

name: no-61
label: No. 61
text:
% Problem 61. Chace vol. II pl. 83 (photograph XXIII, right half), PDF pp. 213-214; Peet pp. 103-104 (Pl. R).
% A table of fractions of fractions, jotted in a blank margin. Each line "a of b is c" is written as
% Multiply b by a. Result c.  Where the scribe left the fractional dot off a numeral, Chace prints a
% whole number, and so does this file (Peet prints them all as fractions). The special ligature sign for
% '6 written without its dot (Chace prints it "6", note 2) is written '6 here, since the sign is not the numeral 6.
No. 61
"2/3 of 2/3 is '3 9."
Multiply 2/3 by 2/3.
Result '3 9.            % Chace: the scribe omitted the fractional dot (9 for '9); Peet: '3 + '9
"'3 of 2/3 is '6 '18."
Multiply 2/3 by '3.
Result '6 '18.          % '6: the special sign for '6 written without its dot; Chace prints it as 6 (note 2); Peet: '6 + '18
"2/3 of '3 is '6 '18."
Multiply '3 by 2/3.
Result '6 '18.          % '6: the special sign without its dot; Chace prints 6 (note 2); Peet: '6 + '18
"2/3 of '6 is '12 36."
Multiply '6 by 2/3.     % '6: the special sign without its dot; Chace prints 6 (note 2); Peet: '6
Result '12 36.          % Chace: the scribe omitted the fractional dot (36 for '36); Peet: '12 + '36
"2/3 of '2 is '3."
Multiply '2 by 2/3.
Result '3.
"'3 of '2 is '6."
Multiply '2 by '3.
Result '6.
"'6 of '2 is '12."
Multiply '2 by '6.      % Chace note 4: this '6 is an unusual sign, like the 6 of 2 ÷ 37; the apparent stroke may be a crack or a pen slip
Result '12.
"'12 of '2 is 24."
Multiply '2 by '12.
Result 24.              % Chace: the scribe omitted the fractional dot (24 for '24); Peet: '24
% lines 5-8 were first written in the form of line 9 ("'3, '2 of it is ...") and altered to the form of lines 1-4 (Chace note 3; Peet p. 103)
"'9, 2/3 of it is 18 ['54]."
Multiply '9 by 2/3.
Result 18 ['54].        % Chace: the scribe omitted the fractional dot (18 for '18); '54 restored; Peet: '18 [+ '54]
"'9 of 2/3 is '18 '54,"  % written again in the margin, in the form of lines 1-4 (Chace note 5)
Multiply 2/3 by '9.
Result '18 '54.
[...]                   % Chace: lost lines, about five, "fractions of '9 and '5"; not restored. Peet restores line 10 ['9 ?], line 11 ['9 ?], line 12 ['5, 2/3 of it is '10 + '30]?, line 13 ['5, '3 of it is '15]?, line 14 ['5, '2 of it is '10]?
"['5], '4 of it is '20."
Multiply ['5] by '4.
Result '20.
"'7, 2/3 of it is '14 42."   % Peet: "2/3 <of it>" (words omitted by the scribe)
Multiply '7 by 2/3.
Result '14 42.          % Chace: the scribe omitted the fractional dot (42 for '42); Peet: '14 + '4[2] (the 2 restored)
                        % Peet restores beside this line ['3 of it is '21]?; Chace has nothing here
"'7, '2 of it is '14."
Multiply '7 by '2.
Result '14.             % Peet restores beside this line ['4 of it is '28]?; Chace has nothing here
"'11, 2/3 of it is '22 '66; '3 of it is '33."
Multiply '11 by 2/3.
Result '22 '66.
Multiply '11 by '3.
Result '33.
"'11, '2 of it is '22; '4 of it is 44."
Multiply '11 by '2.
Result '22.
Multiply '11 by '4.
Result 44.              % Chace: the scribe omitted the fractional dot (44 for '44); Peet: '44
about: Problem 61. Chace vol. II pl. 83 (photograph XXIII, right half), PDF pp. 213-214; Peet pp. 103-104 (Pl. R).

name: no-61b
label: No. 61B
text:
% Problem 61B. Chace vol. II pl. 83 (photograph XXIII, right half), PDF pp. 213-214; Peet p. 104 (Pl. R).
% A rule in words; the papyrus writes no working.
No. 61B
"The making of 2/3 of a fraction uneven. If is said to thee, What is 2/3 of '5?"
"Make thou times of it 2, times 6 of it; 2/3 of it this is."
"Behold does one according to the like for fraction every uneven which may occur."
about: Problem 61B. Chace vol. II pl. 83 (photograph XXIII, right half), PDF pp. 213-214; Peet p. 104 (Pl. R).
words: The making of 2/3 of a fraction uneven. If is said to thee, What is 2/3 of '5?

name: no-62
label: No. 62
text:
% Problem 62. Chace vol. II pl. 84, PDF pp. 215-216; Peet pp. 104-107 (Pl. R).
No. 62
{"Example of making a bag under precious metals various."}
"If is said to thee, A bag, gold in it, silver in it, lead in it; is bought bag this for sha'ty 84. What is that which there is to precious metal each?"
"As for what is given for gold, a deben, sha'ty 12 this is; for silver sha'ty 6 this is; for lead, a deben, sha'ty 3 this is."
"Add thou what is given for a sha'ty of precious metal each; there become 21."   % Chace: "The scribe should have written dbn [deben] here, not š'ty"; Peet: "ring (sic, read deben)"
"Make thou the 21 for the finding of sha'ty 84; what was bought, this is, in bag this; there become: 4, which assignest thou to precious metal each."
"The doing as it occurs:"
"Multiplies one, this means, 4 up to times 12; there becomes gold: 48; the amount of it this is."
  12   48      % gold; each row is 4 times the multiplier on the left
  6    24      % silver
  3    12      % lead
Total 84.      % the papyrus writes "21  Total  84": the multipliers add to 21
about: Problem 62. Chace vol. II pl. 84, PDF pp. 215-216; Peet pp. 104-107 (Pl. R).
words: If is said to thee, A bag, gold in it, silver in it, lead in it; is bought bag this for sha'ty 84. What is that which there is to precious metal each?

name: no-63
label: No. 63
text:
% Problem 63. Chace vol. II pl. 85 (photographs XXIII-XXIV), PDF pp. 217-218; Peet p. 107 (Pl. S).
% The first three lines were covered by ancient patches; a later hand rewrote what it thought stood there.
No. 63
"[Example of dividing] loaves 700 for man 4, 2/3 to 1, '2 to another ['3 to another, '4 to another]; cause thou that know I the share of one thereof each."
"Add thou 2/3, ['2], '3, '4; there becomes 1 '2 '4."   % Chace: the scribe who wrote on the patches omitted this '2; Peet: <'2> (omitted)
2/3
['2]
'3
'4
Total 1 '2 '4.
"Call thou 1 out of 1 '2 '4; there becomes '2 '14."
Reckon with 1 '2 '4 to find 1.
Result '2 '14.
"Make thou '2 '14 of 700, namely, 400."
Multiply 700 by '2 '14.
Result 400.
"Make thou 2/3 of 400, namely, 266 2/3; '2 of 400, namely, 200; '3 of 400, namely, 133 '3; '4 of 400, namely, 100; the share of one thereof each."
Multiply 400 by 2/3.
Result 266 2/3.
Multiply 400 by '2.
Result 200.
Multiply 400 by '3.
Result 133 '3.
Multiply 400 by '4.
Result 100.
{"The doing as it occurs:"} "The amount, 700."
"'2 '14: 400."
"2/3 of 400 to 1: 266 2/3; '2 of 400 to 1: 200; '3 of 400 to 1: 113 '3; '4 of 400 to 1: 100."
266 2/3
200
113 '3         % Chace: "Mistake for 133"; Peet prints 133 '3 without remark
100
Total 700.
about: Problem 63. Chace vol. II pl. 85 (photographs XXIII-XXIV), PDF pp. 217-218; Peet p. 107 (Pl. S).
words: [Example of dividing] loaves 700 for man 4, 2/3 to 1, '2 to another ['3 to another, '4 to another]; cause thou that know I the share of one thereof each.

name: no-64
label: No. 64
text:
% Problem 64. Chace vol. II pl. 86, PDF pp. 219-220; Peet pp. 107-108 (Pl. S).
No. 64
{"Example of distributing difference."} "If is said to thee, Barley, hekat 10 for man 10, the difference of man each to second his, in barley, hekat '8 this is."
"The share average is: hekat '2."   % Chace: "Mistake for 1"; Peet: "1/2 hekat (read 1 hekat)", "the scribe has here written 1/2 hekat instead of 1"
"Take away 1 from 10; the remainder is: 9."
Take 1 from 10.
Remainder 9.
"Is made '2 of the difference, namely, '16."
Multiply '8 by '2.
Result '16.
"Make up to times 9; there becomes hekat '2 '16."
Multiply '16 by 9.
Result '2 '16.         % in hekat
"Add on to the share average. Take away thou the hekat '8 for man each to include the one under the end."
{"The doing as it occurs:"}
1 '2 '16
1 '4 '8 '16
1 '4 '16
1 '8 '16
1 '16
'2 '4 '8 '16
'2 '4 '16
'2 '8 '16
'2 '16
'4 '8 '16
Total 10.         % the papyrus: "Total 10 hekat" (Peet: strictly the hekat sign should precede if the stroke is 10); the papyrus writes the ten shares in one line; Peet sets them in two rows of five, same order and figures
about: Problem 64. Chace vol. II pl. 86, PDF pp. 219-220; Peet pp. 107-108 (Pl. S).
words: The share average is: hekat '2.

name: no-65
label: No. 65
text:
% Problem 65. Chace vol. II pl. 87, PDF pp. 221-222; Peet p. 109 (Pl. S).
No. 65
{"Example of making loaves 100 for man 10;"} "a boatman, a foreman, one at the door, with double."
"The working-out of it: Add thou the people supplied; there become 13."
"Operate on 13 for the finding of the loaves 100; there become 7 2/3 '39."
Reckon with 13 to find 100.
Result 7 2/3 '39.
"Say thou, The eating, this is, of the man 7, and the boatman, the foreman, the one at the door, with double."
% the papyrus sets the seven single shares in two columns (four, then three), and the three double shares beside them
7 2/3 '39
7 2/3 39        % Chace: "The scribe omitted the fractional dot" (39 for '39); Peet: 7 2/3 + '39
7 2/3 '39
7 2/3 '39
7 2/3 '39
7 2/3 '39
7 2/3 '39
15 '3 '26 '78   % the boatman
15 '3 '26 '78   % the foreman
15 '3 '26 '78   % the one at the door
Total 100.
about: Problem 65. Chace vol. II pl. 87, PDF pp. 221-222; Peet p. 109 (Pl. S).
words: The working-out of it: Add thou the people supplied; there become 13.

name: no-66
label: No. 66
text:
% Problem 66. Chace vol. II pl. 88, PDF pp. 223-224; Peet pp. 109-110 (Pl. S).
No. 66
{"Fat, hekat 10,"} "goes out for a year; what is the share of a day therein?"
"The working-out of it: Make thou the fat, hekat 10, in ro; there become 3200."   % Chace: the scribe first omitted "hekat 10" and added it above the line
"Make thou the year in days; there become 365."
"Call thou 3200 out of 365; there become 8 2/3 '10 '2190, making in ro: '64 3 ro 2/3 '10 '2190; the share of a day this is."   % Chace: "m r'w [in ro] is not accurately used since we have first a fraction of a hekat"; Peet: "making in ro (sic) '64 hekat and (3 2/3 '10 '2190) ro"
{"The doing as it occurs:"}
Reckon with 365 to find 3200.
  1      365
  2      730
  4      1460
  [8]    [2920]     % Chace restores this row in brackets; Peet: "8  2920 has been omitted after 4  1460"
  2/3    243 '3
  '10    36 '2
  '2190  '6
{"Total 8 2/3 '10 '2190."}   % red. A total of the multipliers 8, 2/3, '10, '2190, not of the products, and no row is ticked; the notation's Total adds products, so it is kept as words (independent review, finding 6)
"Shalt do thou according to the like in relation to what is said to thee, all, like example this."
about: Problem 66. Chace vol. II pl. 88, PDF pp. 223-224; Peet pp. 109-110 (Pl. S).
words: The working-out of it: Make thou the fat, hekat 10, in ro; there become 3200.

name: no-67
label: No. 67
text:
% Problem 67. Chace vol. II pl. 89, PDF pp. 225-226; Peet pp. 110-111 (Pl. T).
No. 67
{"Example of reckoning the dues of a herdsman."} "Now then came herdsman this to the cattle-numbering under cattle 70. Said accountant this of cattle to herdsman this, Small indeed is cattle-amount (?) this that hast brought thou. Is then where the cattle-amount (?) of thine great?"
"Said herdsman this to him, What have brought I to thee is: 2/3 of '3 of the cattle which hast committed thou to me. Count for me and wilt find thou me complete am I."
{"The doing as it occurs:"}
  1     1
  2/3   2/3
  '3    '3
"2/3 of '3 of it: '6 '18."
Multiply '3 by 2/3.
Result '6 '18.
"Call thou 1 out of '6 '18."   % '6: the special sign for '6 without its dot; Chace prints 6 (note 12)
Reckon with '6 '18 to find 1.  % '6: the special sign without its dot (Chace: 6)
  1     '6 '18     % '6: the special sign without its dot (Chace: 6); Peet: '6 + '18
  2     '3 9       % Chace: "Fractional dot omitted" (9 for '9); Peet: '3 + '9
\ 4     2/3 '6 '18 % '6: the special sign without its dot (Chace: 6); Peet: 2/3 + '6 + '18
\ '2    '9
Total 1.           % the papyrus: "Total 1" (the ticked products)
"The making of 70: Make 70 up to times 4 '2; there become 315. These, this is, which were committed to him."   % Chace: "The making of 70" may be a false start, or read "one multiplies 70"
Multiply 70 by 4 '2.
Result 315.
  1     315
  2/3   210
  '3    105        % Chace: Peet's Plate T puts an f after this fraction by confusion with the 100-sign; "His text is correct"
"2/3 of '3 of it: 70. These, this is, which brought he."
Multiply 105 by 2/3.
Result 70.
about: Problem 67. Chace vol. II pl. 89, PDF pp. 225-226; Peet pp. 110-111 (Pl. T).

name: no-68
label: No. 68
text:
% Problem 68. Chace vol. II pl. 90 (photograph XXV), PDF pp. 227-228; Peet pp. 111-112 (Pl. T).
% The grain is reckoned in quadruple hekat; "hekat" and "ro" below are the quadruple hekat and its
% 320th part. The papyrus writes "ro 2/3" with the ro sign standing for one ro (Chace, note to No. 47),
% written here 1 2/3 ro. A '' ditto mark under "ro" is written as ro.
No. 68
{"If says to thee the scribe,"} "Foremen 4, have received they grain, quadruple hekat great, 100 (hekat)."   % Chace: this hekat-sign is superfluous, and should precede, not follow, the numeral; Peet: 100 quadruple-hekat written with the wrong sign
"Is the gang of the first: man 12."
12      % "The first, man 12"
8       % the second
6       % the third
4       % the fourth
Total 30.
"Make thou the operation on 30 for the finding of 100; there become 3 '3,"
Reckon with 30 to find 100.
Result 3 '3.
"making in grain 3 '4 '16 '64 ro 2/3,"   % = 3 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro
"making: times 12 for the first, 8 the second, 6 the third, 4 the fourth."
  1   3 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro
  2   6 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro         % Chace: this 6 resembles the abstract 6 of 2 ÷ 59; perhaps meant for the special sign for 6 hekat
\ 4   13 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro
\ 8   26 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro
"Total of the first: '4 15."   % hundred-quadruple-hekat notation: '4 of 100 and 15, i.e. 40. Chace prints '4 15; Peet: "Total, the first, 40 hekat"
  1   3 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro
  2   6 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro
  4   13 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro
\ 8   26 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro
"Total: '4 1 '2 '8 '32 3 ro '3, the second."   % hundred notation: '4 of 100 and 1 '2 '8 '32, i.e. 26 '2 '8 '32, and 3 '3 ro; Peet: "Total, (26 '2 '8 '32) hekat + 3 '3 ro, the second"
  1   3 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro        % Chace: Photograph XXV shows finger-prints on a patch here
\ 2   6 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro
  4   13 '4 '16 '64 hekat [1] 2/3 ro     % Chace: the ro (ditto) mark restored ["]; Peet: "sic 4" (no tick) and "+ <1> 2/3 ro"
"Total of the third 20."
  1   3 '4 '16 '64 hekat [1 2/3 ro]      % Chace: the scribe who wrote on the patch omitted 1 2/3 ro here; restored
  2   6 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro
\ 4   13 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro
"Total of the fourth: 13 '4 '16 '64 ro [2/3]."   % Chace: the ro (ditto) mark is there, the 2/3 omitted on the patch and restored; Peet: "[+ 1 2/3 ro]" (all restored), though his Plate T gives the sign for one ro
{"List of these:"} "Foremen; Barley, quadruple hekat great."   % Chace: "barley"; by a slip Peet uses "corn"
"The first 12: '4 15, 40."
"The second 8: '4 1 '2 '8 '32 3 ro '3, 26 2/3."
"The third 6: 20, 20."
"The fourth 4: 13 '4 '16 '64 ro 2/3, 13 '3."
"Total 30: 100 hekat, 100 hekat."   % Chace: the scribe should have omitted the hekat-sign in the last column, which is not in hekat; Peet agrees ("should of course be omitted")
40
26 2/3
20
13 '3
Total 100.

name: no-69
label: No. 69
text:
% Problem 69. Chace vol. II pl. 91, PDF pp. 229-230; Peet pp. 114-116 (Pl. U).
% Chace prints the proof of the pefsu (plate operation d), the reduction to ro (e) and the final proof (f)
% in a column on the right, and notes (note 3) that d and e belong after the statement of the pefsu;
% they are written here in that order, as in Chace vol. I and Peet.
No. 69
{"Meal, hekat 3 '2,"} "made into loaves 80. Cause thou that know I the amount of a unit therefrom in meal, cause thou that know I the pefsu of them."
"Make thou the operation on 3 '2 for the finding of 80."
Reckon with 3 '2 to find 80.
  1     3 '2
  10    35
\ 20    70
\ 2     7
\ 2/3   2 '3
\ '21   '6
\ '7    '2
"The pefsu is 22 2/3 '7 '21."
Result 22 2/3 '7 '21.
% operation d: proof of the pefsu (the sum, 80, is not written)
\ 1     22 2/3 '7 '21
\ 2     45 '3 '4 '14 '28 '42
\ '2    11 '3 '14 '42
% operation e
\ 1     320
\ 2     640
\ '2    160

"The doing as it occurs:"
  1     80
\ 10    800
  2     160
\ 4     320
Total 1120.
"As for the amount of a unit of the loaves in meal, '32 4 ro [this is]."   % Chace: "The scribe omitted the word pw at the end of this sentence"
% operation f: proof; a ditto mark alone under "ro" stands for one ro
  1     '32 hekat 4 ro
  2     '16 '64 hekat 3 ro
  4     '8 '32 '64 hekat 1 ro

  32    1 '4 '8 '64 hekat 3 ro
\ 64    2 '2 '4 '32 '64 hekat 1 ro
"There becomes meal: hekat 3 '2."
Total 3 '2 hekat.   % the papyrus: "There becomes", not "Total"

No. 70
{"Meal, hekat 7 '2 '4 '8,"} "made into loaves 100. What is the basis of a unit of the loaves therefrom in meal? What is the pefsu of them?"   % Chace: a special hieratic sign for 7 hekat; Peet: "the unusual hieratic form of the numeral 7"
"Make thou the operation on 7 '2 '4 '8 for the finding of 100."

name: no-71
label: No. 71
text:
% Problem 71. Chace vol. II pl. 93, PDF pp. 233-234; Peet pp. 117-118 (Pl. U).
No. 71
{"Beer, des 1;"} "'4 of it has been poured off, then has been it diluted with water. Has been weakened it to pefsu what?"
"Make thou the des 1 in besha; there becomes besha '2."   % Chace (after Peet p. 117): the scribe forgot to repeat the hekat sign after the determinative of besha, and used the ordinary sign for '2 instead of the Horus-eye '2 hekat; Peet: "a scribe's error in the second line"
"Take away thou '4 of it, namely, '8;"
Multiply '2 by '4.
Result '8.
"the remainder is: '4 '8."
Take '8 from '2.
Remainder '4 '8.
"Make thou '4 '8 for the finding of 1; there become 2 2/3; a pefsu of 2 2/3 this is."
Reckon with '4 '8 to find 1.
Result 2 2/3.
about: Problem 71. Chace vol. II pl. 93, PDF pp. 233-234; Peet pp. 117-118 (Pl. U).
words: Make thou the des 1 in besha; there becomes besha '2.

name: no-72
label: No. 72
text:
% Problem 72. Chace vol. II pl. 94, PDF pp. 235-236; Peet pp. 118-119 (Pl. V).
% "Loaves of 10, 100" means 100 loaves of pefsu 10 (Chace note 4).
No. 72
{"Example of exchanging"} "loaves with loaves. If is said to thee, Loaves of 10, 100, exchanged with a number of loaves of 45."
"Make thou the excess of 45 as to 10; there become 35."
Take 10 from 45.
Remainder 35.
"Make thou 10 for the finding of 35; there become 3 '2."
Reckon with 10 to find 35.
Result 3 '2.
"Make thou 100 up to times 3 '2; there become 350."   % Chace: there may be an erased vertical stroke after sp (Peet, Plate V, note b)
Multiply 100 by 3 '2.
Result 350.
"Add thou 100 to it; there become 450."
350
100
Total 450.
"Say thou, The exchange this is: the loaves of 10, 100, with loaves of 45, 450, making in wedyet-flour 10 hekat."   % Peet (p. 119): the plural strokes of wedyet omitted by confusion with the hekat sign; Chace disagrees (note 12)
about: Problem 72. Chace vol. II pl. 94, PDF pp. 235-236; Peet pp. 118-119 (Pl. V).
words: Make thou the excess of 45 as to 10; there become 35.

name: no-73
label: No. 73
text:
% Problem 73. Chace vol. II pl. 95, PDF pp. 237-238; Peet p. 119 (Pl. V).
No. 73
{"If is said to thee,"} "Loaves of 10, 100, exchanged with pefsu 15; how many is this for the exchange of them?"
"Make thou the basis of the loaves 100 in wedyet-flour, namely, (ky t'w 10) [10 hekat]."   % Chace: "the words in the parenthesis do not belong here" (copied from the opening of No. 76), and "10 hekat" was not written; Peet: the scribe's eye wandered to the opening words of No. 76; restores [namely 10 hekat]
"Make thou 10 up to times 15; there become 150."
Multiply 10 by 15.
Result 150.
"Say thou, The exchange of them this is."
"The doing as it occurs: Loaves of 10, 100, exchanged with loaves of 15, [r] 150; 10 hekat."   % the final 10 hekat is written as a stroke (Peet); Chace restores an r before 150
about: Problem 73. Chace vol. II pl. 95, PDF pp. 237-238; Peet p. 119 (Pl. V).
words: Make thou the basis of the loaves 100 in wedyet-flour, namely, (ky t'w 10) [10 hekat].

name: no-74
label: No. 74
text:
% Problem 74. Chace vol. II pl. 96, PDF pp. 239-240; Peet pp. 119-120 (Pl. V).
% "Loaves of 5, 1000" means 1000 loaves of pefsu 5; "10 and 20" means loaves of pefsu 10 and 20 (Chace notes 1, 2).
No. 74
{"Another."} "Loaves of 5, 1000, exchanged with 10 and 20; what is the exchange of them?"   % "10 r 20": Chace: "evidently means loaves of pefsu 10 and 20"; Peet: the scribe "has evidently failed to see that the 10 and 20 are both pfsw", so the r-sign is not needed
"Value thou the loaves of 5, 1000; there becomes, Upper Egyptian barley, 200 hekat. Say thou, The wedyet-flour this is."
"Make thou '2 of 200 hekat, namely, 100 hekat."
Multiply 200 by '2.
Result 100.
"Make thou 100 hekat times 10; there become 1000; the amount, this is, of pefsu 10."
Multiply 100 by 10.
Result 1000.
"Make thou the 100 hekat up to times 20; there become 2000; the amount, this is, of pefsu 20."   % Chace: the scribe wrote the masculine article here, though numeral and noun are feminine
Multiply 100 by 20.
Result 2000.
"The doing as it occurs: Loaves of 5, 1000, making in wedyet-flour 200 hekat;"
"the exchange: 10, 1000, 100 (hekat); 20, 2000, 100 (hekat)."   % the papyrus sets these in columns, with ditto marks for "the exchange" and "hekat"
about: Problem 74. Chace vol. II pl. 96, PDF pp. 239-240; Peet pp. 119-120 (Pl. V).
words: Value thou the loaves of 5, 1000; there becomes, Upper Egyptian barley, 200 hekat. Say thou, The wedyet-flour this is.

name: no-75
label: No. 75
text:
% Problem 75. Chace vol. II pl. 97, PDF pp. 241-242; Peet p. 120 (Pl. V).
No. 75
{"Another."} "Loaves of 20, 155, exchanged with pefsu 30."   % Chace: the plural strokes, omitted in the B.M. Facsimile, led Peet to omit them on his Plate V
"Make thou the loaves of 20, 155, in wedyet-flour; hekat 7 '2 '4 this is."   % Chace and Peet: the special sign for 7 hekat (unusual form of 7)
"Make up to times 30; there become 232 '2."
Multiply 7 '2 '4 by 30.
Result 232 '2.
"The doing as it occurs: Loaves of 20, 155, making in wedyet-flour 7 '2 '4, exchanged with 30, 232 '2, 7 '2 '4."
about: Problem 75. Chace vol. II pl. 97, PDF pp. 241-242; Peet p. 120 (Pl. V).
words: Make thou the loaves of 20, 155, in wedyet-flour; hekat 7 '2 '4 this is.

name: no-76
label: No. 76
text:
% Problem 76. Chace vol. II pl. 98, PDF pp. 243-244; Peet pp. 120-121 (Pl. V).
No. 76
{"Another."} "Loaves of 10, 1000, exchanged with a number of loaves of 20 and 30. Shall hear he."
"'20 '30"          % heading of the two numbers below (Peet: '20 over 1 '2, '30 over 1)
1 '2
1
Total 2 '2.
"Make for the finding of 30."
Reckon with 2 '2 to find 30.
  1     2 '2
\ 10    25
\ 2     5
Result 12.          % the papyrus: "Total 12"
"Make thou the basis of the loaves 1000 in wedyet-flour, in hekat: 100 hekat. Make times 12; what results therefrom this is: 1200."
Multiply 100 by 12.
Result 1200.
"The exchange of it is: 20 and 30."
"Loaves of 10, 1000, making in wedyet-flour 100 hekat."
"20: 1200, '2 10."  % hundred-quadruple-hekat notation: '2 of 100 and 10, i.e. 60 hekat; Peet: "60 hekat"
"30: 1200, '4 15."  % '4 of 100 and 15, i.e. 40; Peet: "40 hekat". Chace: "The diagonal stroke at the base of the sign for 5 hekat is a mistake"
about: Problem 76. Chace vol. II pl. 98, PDF pp. 243-244; Peet pp. 120-121 (Pl. V).

name: no-77
label: No. 77
text:
% Problem 77. Chace vol. II pl. 99, PDF pp. 245-246; Peet p. 121 (Pl. V).
No. 77
{"Example of"} "exchanging beer with loaves. If is said to thee, Beer, des 10, exchanged with pefsu 5."
"Make thou the beer des 10 in wedyet-flour, 5 this is."
"Make thou the hekat 5 times 5; there become 25."
Multiply 5 by 5.
Result 25.
"Say thou the exchange of it this is."
"The doing as it occurs: Beer, des 10, wedyet-flour, hekat 5, exchanged with loaves of 5, 25, 5."
about: Problem 77. Chace vol. II pl. 99, PDF pp. 245-246; Peet p. 121 (Pl. V).

name: no-78
label: No. 78
text:
% Problem 78. Chace vol. II pl. 100, PDF pp. 247-248; Peet p. 121 (Pl. W).
No. 78
{"Example of"} "exchanging loaves with beer. If is said to thee, Loaves of 10, 100, exchanged with a quantity of beer of 2."   % Chace: the scribe first omitted the word "exchanging" and added it above the line
"Make thou the loaves of 10, 100, in wedyet-flour; 10 hekat this is."
"Make times 2; what results therefrom this is: 20."
Multiply 10 by 2.
Result 20.
"Say thou the exchange of it this is."
about: Problem 78. Chace vol. II pl. 100, PDF pp. 247-248; Peet p. 121 (Pl. W).

% Problem 80. Chace vol. II pl. 102, PDF pp. 251-252; Peet pp. 122-123 (Pl. W).

No. 80

name: no-82
label: No. 82
text:
% Problem 82. Chace vol. II pl. 104 (photograph XXVI), PDF pp. 255-256; Peet pp. 124-125 (Pl. X).
% Large amounts are in the hundred-hekat notation: Chace prints e.g. "'2 10 '4 8" (half of 100, 10,
% a quarter of 100, 8 = 93). The quoted lines keep Chace's printing; the values in hekat are in the notes
% and in the subtraction below, which the papyrus states as "taken away" and "remainder".
No. 82
{"Estimate of the food of a fowl-yard,"} "made in loaves as the portion of a day."
"Goose fatted eats, bird 10, wedyet-flour 2 '2;"
"Making for day 10: 25;"
"Making for day 40: 100 hekat."
"That which is to be ground to produce (?) it is spelt: hekat 100 hekat '2 10 6 '2 '8 '32 3 ro '3,"   % = 166 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro (Peet the same)
"wheat: '3 '4 8 '4 '16 '64 ro 2/3."   % = 66 '3 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro. Chace: the special sign for 8 hekat here and in the next lines; Peet: "the unique use here of [the hundred sign with '3] to represent 33 '3 hekat"
"That which is to be taken away according to '10 is 6 '2 '8 '32 3 ro '3."
"The remainder, which is to be given, is '2 10 '4 8 '4 '16 '64 ro 2/3;"   % = 93 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro. Chace: the sign for 10 hekat precedes the '4-sign for 25 hekat
Take 6 '2 '8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro from 100 hekat.
Remainder 93 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro.
"Making in grain in hekat, '2 10 '4 8 '4 '16 '64 ro 2/3;"   % = 93 '4 '16 '64 hekat 1 2/3 ro
"Making in double hekat, 20 '4 2 '2 '4 '64 3 ro '3."   % = 47 '2 '4 '64 hekat 3 '3 ro. Chace: "Mistakes ... are corrected in volume 1"; Peet: halving 93 '3 gives 46 2/3 double-hekat, "wrongly given as (47 '2 '4 '64) hekat + 3 '3 ro"
about: Problem 82. Chace vol. II pl. 104 (photograph XXVI), PDF pp. 255-256; Peet pp. 124-125 (Pl. X).
words: Goose fatted eats, bird 10, wedyet-flour 2 '2;

name: no-82b
label: No. 82B
text:
% Problem 82B. Chace vol. II pl. 104 (photograph XXVI), PDF pp. 255-256; Peet p. 125 (Pl. X).
No. 82B
"Amount of a fatted bird, the food of it, bird 10: 1 '4;"
"Making for day 10: 10 2 '4;"   % = 12 '4. Chace: a mistake, corrected in his vol. I; Peet: "12 '4 hekat (read 12 '2)"
"40: '2, 50;"                    % '2 of 100, i.e. 50 hekat
"Making of grain in double hekat, 10 10 3 '2 '4 '8 4 ro '4 '6 '6."   % = 23 '2 '4 '8 hekat 4 '4 '6 '6 ro. Chace: mistake, corrected in vol. I; Peet: "the answer is incorrect; it should be 23 '3 hekat, i.e. (23 '4 '16 '64) hekat + 1 2/3 ro"; "23 ... is written 10 + 13"; '6 '6 "is written for '3 simply" in M.K. hieratic
about: Problem 82B. Chace vol. II pl. 104 (photograph XXVI), PDF pp. 255-256; Peet p. 125 (Pl. X).

name: no-83
label: No. 83
text:
% Problem 83. Chace vol. II pl. 105 (photograph XXVI), PDF pp. 257-258; Peet pp. 125-126 (Pl. X).
No. 83
{"As for the food of goose 4"} "of those that are shut up, barley Lower-Egyptian, a hinu this is;"   % Chace: "the writing of the compound word is evidently corrupt here. It is on a patch"; Peet: line 2 lost and incorrectly restored by the ancient mender; the feminine form "must be wrong"
{"the portion of one of goose is '64 hekat 3 ro."}
{"As for the food of a goose goes it into the pond,"} "barley Lower-Egyptian hekat '16 '32 2 ro, a hinu this is for goose 1;"
"Making for goose 10 barley Lower-Egyptian a hekat;"
"For day 10: hekat 10;"
"For a month: '4 5."   % hundred notation: '4 of 100 and 5, i.e. 30 hekat; Peet: "30 hekat"
{"The portion of a day in food for a goose fatted,"} "it eats"
'8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro    % "bird 1"
'8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro    % a terp-goose, 1
'8 '32 hekat 3 '3 ro    % a crane, 1
'32 '64 hekat 1 ro      % a ser-goose, 1. Chace: the scribe transposed the first consonants of this word and the next (properly sr and s.t). Peet reads this bird as the set-bird
'64 hekat 3 ro          % a set-duck, 1. Peet: ser-bird
3 ro                    % a dove, 1
3 ro                    % a quail, 1
"Total"                 % Chace: "A total, probably of hekat, has been omitted by the Rhind scribe, and perhaps was lacking also in the text from which he copied"; Peet: "Total" (sic)
about: Problem 83. Chace vol. II pl. 105 (photograph XXVI), PDF pp. 257-258; Peet pp. 125-126 (Pl. X).
words: Making for goose 10 barley Lower-Egyptian a hekat;

name: no-84
label: No. 84
text:
% Problem 84. Chace vol. II pl. 106 (photograph XXVI), PDF pp. 259-260; Peet p. 127 (Pl. X).
% Chace agrees with Peet that "with this problem the papyrus reaches its limit of unintelligibility and
% inaccuracy"; Chace follows Peet's readings in the main. Two kinds of food are reckoned side by side;
% each line of the table gives the number of oxen, the first food and the second food, in hekat.
% Large amounts are in the hundred-hekat notation as Chace prints them; values are in the notes.
No. 84
{"Estimate of the food of a stable of oxen."}
"Put down (?), loaves of a hekat."   % heading of the first food column (Peet: "... food")
"Put down common food by the hekat." % heading of the second food column (Peet: "ordinary ... food (?)")
"Ox, that which eat 4 fine one, Upper Egyptian ox: 24 hekat; 2 hekat."
"2 fine one, Upper Egyptian ox: 22 hekat; 6 hekat."   % Chace: the special sign for 6 hekat
